Photo 1 shows a close-up of the side of the assembly with a circular opening/bearing-like area and a threaded port.

No visible Toyota logo, part number plate, or readable model/engine code in the photos.

identity.kind: engine oil pump / balance shaft assembly (Toyota application)

claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars like Toyota Camry (2018–present) and Toyota RAV4.
claims.evidence: Photos show an engine assembly but no readable part number/engine code or vehicle fitment label to confirm Camry/RAV4 (2018+).

risks.risk: Wrong exact part variant (different engine codes/years use different oil pump/balance shaft assemblies).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped/engraved part number and/or any label on the housing (close-up, in focus), plus the engine code from the donor car (e.g., 2AR/2GR/etc.).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not guaranteed to fit the buyer’s exact Toyota model/engine; treated like a mismatch risk.

risks.risk: Internal wear/damage (balance shaft bearings, pump gears/rotor) not visible from outside; could fail soon after installation.
risks.proof: Video of the assembly being rotated/checked (shafts turn smoothly without grinding), and a photo of any wear marks; ideally a bench test result.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: assumed not proven to be in good working condition.

risks.risk: Missing components or incorrect seals/gaskets (common with used assemblies).
risks.proof: Photo of everything included in the package laid out (gaskets, bolts, pickup tube, O-rings) and confirmation of what is included/excluded.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: missing/unknown seals/gaskets; buyer may need replacements.

risks.risk: Contamination or oil leakage (residue may indicate prior leak; could be from cracks/warped surfaces).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of mating surfaces and any cracks, plus a wipe-clean test showing no fresh seepage after a short time.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: possible leak/needs reseal.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the stamped/engraved part number on the housing (make it readable).
Send the donor vehicle details: Toyota model, year, and engine code (or VIN last 6 digits) so fitment can be verified.
Send a short video showing the shafts/gears rotate smoothly (no grinding) and confirm no play/roughness.
List what is included in the sale (gaskets/seals/bolts/pickup tube) and send photos of all included parts laid out.
response.reason: The photos show an engine oil pump/balance shaft-type assembly, but there is no readable part number or fitment identifier to confirm the exact Toyota variant (Camry/RAV4 2018+). Without that, a worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
